Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance has partial oversight over the ID system funding. The 'Tabioucom' digital stamp duty payment platform (launched August 2024) was jointly developed by the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Interior, and Post ministry, and chaired by Finance Minister Laaziz Faid. The platform covers stamp fees for ID cards and passports, indicating MoF involvement in ID-related fiscal matters. However, the primary budget authority for the CNIBE system sits with the Ministry of Interior. No dedicated MoF budget line specifically for the ID system was found in public documents.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed at 2 (Partial oversight). The original algeriainvest.com source checks out and is corroborated: the Finance Ministry (DGI) jointly launched the 'Tabioucom' e-payment platform for ID/passport/licence stamp duties in Aug 2024, and Finance Law texts (e.g. PLFC 2018, reported by TSA and Algerie-Eco) show the Ministry of Finance sets and revises CNIBE issuance fees via the Loi de Finances process. However, primary budget authority and vendor contracting for CNIBE production (e.g. the ~EUR17m Gemalto contract) sits with the Ministry of Interior (Algerie360, 2015), and no dedicated MoF budget line for the ID system itself was found — consistent with 'partial' rather than 'full' oversight. Value Code unchanged; two additional independent sources now corroborate what was previously a single-source score.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The national identity card is mandatory for accessing government social services and administrative programs in Algeria. The card is required for all administrative procedures including enrollment in social protection programs. Algeria's food and energy subsidy system (managed through CNAS and other agencies) requires citizens to be registered, which requires a national ID. The imcra-az.org paper notes that social security account numbers are linked to civil status records and biometric identity systems. No evidence found of social services accessible without a national ID card.

revision_notes: Confirmed at 3 (Mandatory), but on stronger grounds than the original sources (a Wikipedia draft and a low-quality predatory-adjacent journal, imcra-az.org, neither of which is authoritative). Fresher evidence: décret exécutif n° 24-325 (Oct 2024) creating the Allocation Forfaitaire de Solidarité requires a birth certificate/acte de naissance and identity photo per applicant, and the unemployment allowance 'Minha' (décret exécutif n° 22-70) is administered via an ANEM digital platform that cross-checks applicants in real time against the national automated civil-status register — making identity/civil-status verification a hard precondition for benefit payment. This supports 'Mandatory' in substance, though note the sources describe civil-status/decree document requirements rather than an explicit statutory demand to present the physical CNIBE card, so this remains a reasonable but not airtight confirmation — flagged as adequately evidenced rather than certain.
